description: Manage a legal matter from intake to close: open the matter file, track milestones and deadlines, manage documents, and archive when resolved.

steps.description: Receive and log the incoming legal matter request with initial details.

inputs.name: matter-request
inputs.desc: Description of the legal matter or request form

inputs.name: requesting-party
inputs.desc: Person or department requesting legal assistance

outputs.name: matter-summary
outputs.desc: Structured summary of the matter request

outputs.name: matter-type
outputs.desc: Classification of the matter (contract, employment, litigation, regulatory, IP)

process: Extract the key facts from the matter request: parties, subject, urgency, and relevant dates.
Classify the matter by type (contract, employment, litigation, regulatory, IP, or other).
Summarize the request in a structured format suitable for opening a matter file.

steps.description: Open the matter file with all required fields and assign the responsible attorney.

outputs.name: matter-record
outputs.desc: The opened matter file with ID, type, parties, dates, and assigned attorney

outputs.name: key-dates
outputs.desc: List of critical dates and deadlines for the matter

process: Assign a matter ID and create the file with the matter type, parties, and description.
Identify the responsible attorney or team based on matter type and current workload.
Record all known key dates: statute of limitations, filing deadlines, hearing dates, and internal review dates.
Set the initial status and priority level.

steps.description: Track milestones and deadlines throughout the life of the matter.

outputs.name: milestone-status
outputs.desc: Current status of all milestones and upcoming deadlines

outputs.name: overdue-items
outputs.desc: List of any overdue or at-risk milestones

process: Create the milestone schedule from the key dates and add any standard milestones for the matter type.
Track completion of each milestone and flag items approaching their deadline.
Escalate overdue items to the responsible attorney and supervising partner.
Update the matter status as milestones are completed.

steps.description: Manage the document repository for the matter, including filing, versioning, and retrieval.

inputs.name: milestone-status
inputs.desc: Current milestone status to associate documents with phases

outputs.name: document-index
outputs.desc: Index of all documents filed to the matter with metadata

outputs.name: document-status
outputs.desc: Status of document completeness and any gaps

process: Organize the document repository by category (pleadings, correspondence, contracts, evidence, internal memos).
File each document with metadata: date, author, category, and associated milestone.
Track document versions and maintain the audit trail.
Identify any document gaps based on the matter type and milestone requirements.

steps.description: Record the resolution and outcome of the matter.

outputs.name: resolution-record
outputs.desc: Record of the outcome including terms, amounts, and dates

outputs.name: lessons-learned
outputs.desc: Notes on what went well and what to improve for future matters

process: Document the resolution: outcome type (settled, won, lost, withdrawn, expired), terms, and key dates.
Record any financial outcome (settlement amount, judgment, costs, fees recovered).
Note lessons learned and any follow-up obligations.
Update the matter status to resolved.

steps.description: Close the matter file and archive all records per the retention schedule.

outputs.name: closed-matter-record
outputs.desc: The final matter record marked as closed with archive location

outputs.name: retention-schedule
outputs.desc: Retention period and destruction date for the matter file

process: Verify all documents are filed, all time entries billed, and all obligations recorded.
Apply the retention schedule based on matter type and jurisdiction.
Archive the matter file to the designated storage with the retention metadata.
Produce the final closed matter record.

description: Track legal time entries against matters, review for billing compliance, generate pre-bills, and produce invoices.

steps.description: Configure billing rates for attorneys, paralegals, and staff by matter or client.

inputs.name: rate-schedule
inputs.desc: Standard rate schedule for the firm or department

inputs.name: client-billing-agreement
inputs.desc: Any client-specific rate agreements or caps

outputs.name: approved-rates
outputs.desc: The approved billing rates by timekeeper and matter

outputs.name: billing-rules
outputs.desc: Any special billing rules (caps, discounts, block billing restrictions)

process: Load the standard rate schedule by timekeeper level (partner, associate, paralegal, staff).
Apply any client-specific overrides from the billing agreement.
Document the billing rules: maximum hours per task, block billing restrictions, expense caps.
Produce the approved rate card for the matter.

steps.description: Log time entries against matters with descriptions and activity codes.

inputs.name: billing-rules
inputs.desc: Billing rules to apply during entry

outputs.name: time-entries
outputs.desc: Raw time entries with timekeeper, date, hours, description, and activity code

outputs.name: entry-warnings
outputs.desc: Any entries that may violate billing guidelines

process: Record each time entry with: timekeeper, date, matter ID, hours (in tenths), activity code, and narrative description.
Validate each entry against billing rules (minimum increment, block billing, vague descriptions).
Flag entries that may violate client billing guidelines for review.
Calculate the total unbilled time for the period.

steps.description: Review time entries for compliance with billing guidelines before generating the pre-bill.

inputs.name: time-entries
inputs.desc: Raw time entries for the billing period

outputs.name: reviewed-entries
outputs.desc: Time entries that passed compliance review

outputs.name: adjustment-log
outputs.desc: Record of any write-downs, write-offs, or description edits

process: Review each flagged entry for billing guideline compliance.
Edit descriptions that are too vague or contain block billing.
Apply write-downs for excessive time on routine tasks.
Produce the reviewed entry set and the adjustment log.

steps.description: Generate the pre-bill draft for attorney review.

outputs.name: pre-bill
outputs.desc: Draft invoice showing all entries, rates, totals, and expenses

outputs.name: pre-bill-summary
outputs.desc: Summary of total fees, expenses, and adjustments

process: Group entries by matter and timekeeper.
Apply the approved rates to calculate fees for each entry.
Add any reimbursable expenses (filing fees, travel, copying).
Generate the pre-bill with line items, subtotals, and a grand total.

steps.description: Route the pre-bill to the billing attorney for final review and approval.

outputs.name: approved-bill
outputs.desc: The approved invoice after attorney review

outputs.name: approval-notes
outputs.desc: Notes from the billing attorney on any adjustments

process: Send the pre-bill to the billing attorney with the summary.
Record any additional write-downs or description changes requested by the billing attorney.
Apply the final adjustments and mark the bill as approved.
Record the approval in the billing system.

steps.description: Generate and send the final invoice to the client.

outputs.name: sent-invoice
outputs.desc: The final invoice as sent to the client with delivery confirmation

outputs.name: billing-record
outputs.desc: Record of the invoice in the billing system (amount, date, matter, status)

process: Format the invoice per client requirements (LEDES, custom template, standard).
Send the invoice to the client via the agreed delivery method.
Record the invoice in the billing system with status set to outstanding.
Start the payment tracking cycle.

description: Run an e-discovery process from hold through collection, processing, review, and production.

steps.description: Define the scope of the e-discovery effort based on the matter and discovery requests.

inputs.name: discovery-request
inputs.desc: The discovery request, subpoena, or regulatory demand

inputs.name: matter-context
inputs.desc: Background on the legal matter and relevant parties

outputs.name: scope-document
outputs.desc: Defined scope including custodians, date range, data sources, and search terms

outputs.name: custodian-list
outputs.desc: List of custodians whose data must be collected

process: Analyze the discovery request to identify the subject matter, date range, and relevant parties.
Identify the custodians (people whose data may be responsive).
Map the data sources for each custodian (email, documents, chat, cloud storage, mobile).
Define the preliminary search terms and produce the scope document.

steps.description: Collect and preserve data from the identified sources in a forensically sound manner.

outputs.name: collected-data-inventory
outputs.desc: Inventory of all collected data with chain of custody metadata

outputs.name: collection-log
outputs.desc: Log of collection actions, dates, and methods

process: Issue preservation instructions to IT and custodians.
Collect data from each source using forensically sound methods.
Record the chain of custody for each collection (who, when, what, how).
Verify the integrity of collected data with hash values.

steps.description: Process collected data: deduplicate, filter by date range, and extract text and metadata.

outputs.name: processed-data-set
outputs.desc: Deduplicated, filtered data set ready for review

outputs.name: processing-report
outputs.desc: Statistics on data volumes before and after processing

process: Ingest the collected data into the processing platform.
Deduplicate by hash across all custodians.
Apply date range and file type filters from the scope document.
Extract text, metadata, and embedded content for review.

steps.description: Review documents for responsiveness to the discovery request and privilege.

outputs.name: review-results
outputs.desc: Documents tagged as responsive, non-responsive, or privileged

outputs.name: privilege-log
outputs.desc: Log of documents withheld on privilege grounds

process: Apply search terms and analytics to prioritize documents for review.
Review documents for responsiveness to the discovery request.
Identify and tag privileged documents (attorney-client, work product).
Produce the privilege log with the required entries (date, author, recipient, subject, privilege asserted).

steps.description: Format and produce responsive documents to the requesting party.

inputs.name: privilege-log
inputs.desc: Privilege log to accompany the production

outputs.name: production-set
outputs.desc: Final production set with Bates numbers and load file

outputs.name: production-record
outputs.desc: Record of the production (date, volume, format, delivery method)

process: Apply Bates numbering to all responsive documents.
Redact any partially privileged documents.
Generate the production in the agreed format (native, TIFF, PDF) with the load file.
Deliver the production and produce the production record.

description: Manage litigation holds from trigger through release: issue notices, track acknowledgments, and maintain the hold.

steps.description: Assess the hold trigger and determine whether a litigation hold is required.

inputs.name: trigger-event
inputs.desc: The event triggering the hold assessment (lawsuit, demand letter, investigation, regulatory inquiry)

inputs.name: matter-details
inputs.desc: Details about the underlying matter or dispute

outputs.name: hold-decision
outputs.desc: Decision on whether to issue a hold and the rationale

outputs.name: hold-scope
outputs.desc: Scope of the hold: custodians, data types, and date range

process: Evaluate the trigger event to determine whether a duty to preserve exists.
Define the scope of the hold: which custodians, what data types, and what date range.
Document the rationale for the hold decision.
If no hold is required, document the reasons and close.

steps.description: Draft and issue the litigation hold notice to all identified custodians.

inputs.name: hold-decision
inputs.desc: The decision to issue a hold

inputs.name: hold-scope
inputs.desc: Scope including custodians and data types

outputs.name: hold-notice
outputs.desc: The issued hold notice with instructions for custodians

outputs.name: distribution-list
outputs.desc: List of custodians who received the notice with delivery dates

process: Draft the hold notice: explain the preservation obligation, what data to preserve, and what actions to avoid.
Send the notice to all custodians and to IT for system-level preservation.
Record the distribution date and method for each recipient.
Send a copy to the matter file.

steps.description: Track custodian acknowledgments of the hold notice and follow up on non-responses.

outputs.name: acknowledgment-status
outputs.desc: Status of each custodian's acknowledgment (received, pending, escalated)

outputs.name: non-responders
outputs.desc: List of custodians who have not acknowledged

process: Track acknowledgments as they are received from custodians.
Send reminders to custodians who have not acknowledged within the deadline.
Escalate non-responders to their manager and to legal leadership.
Record all acknowledgments and follow-up actions.

steps.description: Send periodic reminders to custodians to maintain the hold.

inputs.name: hold-scope
inputs.desc: Scope of the hold for reminder content

outputs.name: reminder-log
outputs.desc: Log of all reminders sent with dates and recipients

outputs.name: hold-compliance-status
outputs.desc: Overall compliance status of the hold

process: Schedule periodic reminders (quarterly or as required by policy).
Send the reminder to all active custodians reaffirming the preservation obligation.
Track any custodian departures or role changes and update the hold accordingly.
Produce the hold compliance status report.

steps.description: Release the litigation hold when authorized and document the release.

outputs.name: release-notice
outputs.desc: The hold release notice sent to all custodians

outputs.name: hold-management-record
outputs.desc: Complete record of the hold from trigger through release

process: Obtain authorization to release the hold from the responsible attorney.
Draft and send the release notice to all custodians and IT.
Compile the complete hold management record (trigger, notices, acknowledgments, reminders, release).
Archive the record in the matter file.

description: Manage contracts from initial request through drafting, negotiation, execution, obligation tracking, and renewal.

steps.description: Receive and log the contract request with the business requirements.

inputs.name: contract-request
inputs.desc: The request for a new contract or amendment

inputs.name: business-requirements
inputs.desc: The business terms and objectives for the contract

outputs.name: request-record
outputs.desc: Logged request with type, parties, timeline, and business terms

outputs.name: template-recommendation
outputs.desc: Recommended contract template based on the request type

process: Log the request with the requesting party, contract type, and timeline.
Identify the counterparty and any existing relationship or agreements.
Select the appropriate template based on the contract type.
Flag any non-standard terms requested by the business.

steps.description: Draft the contract from the template and business requirements.

inputs.name: request-record
inputs.desc: The logged request with business terms

outputs.name: draft-contract
outputs.desc: The initial draft contract

outputs.name: key-terms-summary
outputs.desc: Summary of key terms for review (pricing, term, liability, IP, termination)

process: Populate the template with the deal-specific terms (parties, pricing, scope, dates).
Adjust clauses to reflect the business requirements and risk tolerance.
Summarize the key terms for stakeholder review.
Send the draft for internal review before sharing with the counterparty.

steps.description: Track the negotiation of contract terms between the parties.

inputs.name: key-terms-summary
inputs.desc: Key terms for reference during negotiation

outputs.name: negotiated-contract
outputs.desc: The contract with all negotiated changes incorporated

outputs.name: negotiation-log
outputs.desc: Log of all redline exchanges, positions, and concessions

process: Send the draft to the counterparty and track the redline exchange.
Log each round of changes: what was proposed, accepted, rejected, or countered.
Escalate sticking points to the business sponsor for guidance on acceptable concessions.
Produce the final negotiated version when both parties agree on all terms.

steps.description: Route the negotiated contract through the internal approval chain.

outputs.name: approved-contract
outputs.desc: The contract approved for execution

outputs.name: approval-record
outputs.desc: Record of all approvals with dates and any conditions

process: Identify the required approvers based on contract value, type, and risk level.
Route the contract with the key terms summary and negotiation log.
Track approval status and follow up on pending approvals.
Record all approvals and any conditions imposed.

steps.description: Execute the contract and file the fully signed version.

inputs.name: approved-contract
inputs.desc: The approved contract ready for signatures

outputs.name: executed-contract
outputs.desc: The fully executed contract with all signatures

outputs.name: obligation-schedule
outputs.desc: Schedule of key obligations, milestones, and dates from the contract

process: Send the contract for signature (wet ink or e-signature).
Collect all signatures and verify execution.
Extract the key obligations and dates into the obligation schedule.
File the executed contract in the contract management system.

steps.description: Track contract renewals and amendments through the lifecycle.

outputs.name: renewal-action
outputs.desc: The renewal decision and any amendments

outputs.name: lifecycle-record
outputs.desc: Complete lifecycle record of the contract from request through current status

process: Monitor the obligation schedule for upcoming renewal and termination dates.
Send renewal reminders to the business sponsor in advance of the notice period.
Process the renewal decision: renew, renegotiate, or terminate.
Update the lifecycle record with the renewal action and any amendments.

description: Triage incoming legal requests: classify by matter type, assess urgency, assign to the appropriate team, and set response expectations.

steps.description: Receive the incoming legal request from any channel and log it.

inputs.name: incoming-request
inputs.desc: The legal request from email, form, phone, or in-person

inputs.name: requester-info
inputs.desc: Information about the person or department making the request

outputs.name: logged-request
outputs.desc: The request logged with a tracking ID, date, and source channel

outputs.name: initial-category
outputs.desc: Preliminary category based on request content

process: Log the request with a unique tracking ID, date, requester, and source channel.
Extract the key details: what happened, who is involved, any deadlines or urgency.
Assign a preliminary category based on keywords and request type.
Acknowledge receipt to the requester.

steps.description: Classify the request by matter type and assess its urgency and complexity.

outputs.name: matter-classification
outputs.desc: Final classification (contract, employment, litigation, regulatory, IP, general)

outputs.name: urgency-assessment
outputs.desc: Urgency level (critical, high, standard, low) with rationale

process: Review the request details to confirm or correct the preliminary category.
Assess urgency based on deadlines, legal exposure, and business impact.
Assess complexity based on matter type, parties involved, and jurisdictions.
Produce the final classification and urgency assessment.

steps.description: Assign the request to the appropriate attorney or team based on classification and workload.

outputs.name: assignment-record
outputs.desc: Record of the assignment: attorney, team, and expected response date

outputs.name: response-timeline
outputs.desc: Expected response and resolution timeline communicated to the requester

process: Match the matter type and complexity to the appropriate practice group or attorney.
Check current workload to balance assignments.
Set the expected response time based on urgency level.
Notify the assigned attorney and communicate the timeline to the requester.

steps.description: Review intake quality and report on request volumes, response times, and assignment patterns.

outputs.name: intake-metrics
outputs.desc: Metrics on request volume, category distribution, average response time, and SLA compliance

outputs.name: intake-record
outputs.desc: Complete intake record for the request

process: Track whether the committed response timeline was met.
Aggregate intake metrics: volume by category, urgency distribution, average assignment time.
Identify bottlenecks or categories with consistently slow response.
Produce the intake record and metrics report.

description: Track regulatory compliance obligations across jurisdictions: inventory regulations, map requirements, assign owners, and monitor completion.

steps.description: Inventory all applicable regulations by jurisdiction and business area.

inputs.name: business-profile
inputs.desc: Description of the business activities, jurisdictions, and regulated areas

inputs.name: existing-inventory
inputs.desc: Any existing list of regulations being tracked

outputs.name: regulation-inventory
outputs.desc: Complete inventory of applicable regulations with citation, jurisdiction, and business area

outputs.name: gap-list
outputs.desc: Regulations not previously tracked that should be

process: Map the business activities to the applicable regulatory bodies and frameworks.
Inventory each applicable regulation with its citation, jurisdiction, and enforcement agency.
Compare against the existing inventory to identify gaps.
Produce the complete regulation inventory and gap list.

steps.description: Map each regulation to its specific compliance requirements.

outputs.name: requirement-map
outputs.desc: Each regulation mapped to its specific compliance requirements (filings, reports, controls, training)

outputs.name: deadline-schedule
outputs.desc: Schedule of all compliance deadlines

process: For each regulation, identify the specific compliance obligations (filings, reporting, controls, training, audits).
Note the frequency and deadlines for each obligation.
Identify overlapping requirements across regulations to avoid duplication.
Produce the requirement map and deadline schedule.

steps.description: Assign an owner and deadline to each compliance requirement.

outputs.name: assigned-obligations
outputs.desc: Each obligation assigned to an owner with a due date

outputs.name: accountability-matrix
outputs.desc: RACI matrix for compliance obligations

process: Identify the natural owner for each obligation based on business function.
Assign primary and backup owners.
Set internal deadlines with enough lead time before the regulatory deadline.
Build the accountability matrix and distribute to all owners.

steps.description: Monitor completion status and escalate overdue items.

outputs.name: compliance-dashboard
outputs.desc: Current status of all obligations (complete, in progress, overdue, upcoming)

outputs.name: escalation-report
outputs.desc: Overdue or at-risk items with escalation actions taken

process: Track completion as owners mark obligations done.
Send reminders for upcoming deadlines.
Escalate overdue items to the owner's manager and to the compliance officer.
Produce the compliance dashboard and escalation report.

steps.description: Produce the periodic compliance report for leadership.

outputs.name: compliance-report
outputs.desc: Periodic compliance report showing overall health, completed items, risks, and trends

outputs.name: compliance-tracker-record
outputs.desc: Complete record of the compliance tracking period

process: Summarize the compliance status: percentage complete, on-time rate, overdue count.
Highlight any material compliance risks or failures.
Note regulatory changes that may affect future obligations.
Produce the report for leadership review.

description: Conduct legal research on a defined question and produce a research memo with analysis and conclusion.

steps.description: Define the legal research question and the relevant jurisdiction and area of law.

inputs.name: research-request
inputs.desc: The legal question or issue to research

inputs.name: matter-context
inputs.desc: Context about the matter that prompted the research

outputs.name: research-question
outputs.desc: The precisely framed legal question

outputs.name: research-scope
outputs.desc: Jurisdiction, area of law, and any constraints on the research

process: Clarify the question: what specific legal issue needs to be answered.
Identify the relevant jurisdiction (federal, state, local, international).
Identify the area of law (contract, tort, employment, regulatory, IP, tax).
Define any constraints: budget, deadline, depth of analysis.

steps.description: Search primary and secondary legal sources for authorities relevant to the question.

outputs.name: source-collection
outputs.desc: Collection of relevant statutes, cases, regulations, and secondary sources

outputs.name: search-log
outputs.desc: Log of databases searched, search terms used, and results

process: Search for relevant statutes and regulations in the identified jurisdiction.
Search for case law interpreting those statutes and addressing the legal question.
Search secondary sources (treatises, law reviews, practice guides) for analysis.
Log all searches and organize the results by relevance.

steps.description: Analyze the collected authorities and develop the legal analysis.

outputs.name: legal-analysis
outputs.desc: Analysis of the applicable authorities and how they apply to the facts

outputs.name: conclusion
outputs.desc: The answer to the research question with confidence level

process: Identify the controlling authorities (binding statutes, regulations, and case law).
Analyze how the authorities apply to the specific facts of the matter.
Address any conflicting authorities or open questions.
Formulate the conclusion and assess the confidence level.

steps.description: Write the research memo in the standard format.

outputs.name: research-memo
outputs.desc: The completed legal research memo (question, brief answer, discussion, conclusion)

outputs.name: memo-record
outputs.desc: Record of the memo in the matter file

process: Write the question presented section.
Write the brief answer summarizing the conclusion in one or two sentences.
Write the discussion section with the detailed legal analysis and citations.
Write the conclusion with any recommendations or caveats.
File the memo in the matter repository.

description: Manage a dispute from initial claim through resolution: assess merits, select the resolution path, execute, and document the outcome.

steps.description: Assess the incoming claim or complaint for merits and exposure.

inputs.name: claim-details
inputs.desc: The claim, complaint, or demand received

inputs.name: internal-facts
inputs.desc: Internal facts and documentation relevant to the dispute

outputs.name: merits-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of the strength of the claim and the defense

outputs.name: exposure-estimate
outputs.desc: Estimated financial and non-financial exposure

process: Analyze the claim: what is alleged, what relief is sought, and what is the legal basis.
Review the internal facts and documentation that support or undermine the claim.
Assess the strength of the claim and the available defenses.
Estimate the financial exposure (damages, costs, fees) and non-financial risks (reputation, precedent).

steps.description: Select the resolution path based on the merits assessment and business objectives.

inputs.name: merits-assessment
inputs.desc: Assessment of claim strength and defenses

outputs.name: selected-path
outputs.desc: The selected resolution path (direct negotiation, mediation, arbitration, litigation)

outputs.name: resolution-strategy
outputs.desc: Strategy for the selected path including goals and settlement authority

process: Evaluate the resolution options: direct negotiation, mediation, arbitration, or litigation.
Consider cost, time, confidentiality, precedent, and business relationship factors.
Obtain settlement authority from the business if negotiation or mediation is selected.
Document the selected path and strategy.

steps.description: Execute the selected resolution process.

outputs.name: process-log
outputs.desc: Log of actions taken during the resolution process

outputs.name: preliminary-outcome
outputs.desc: Preliminary outcome or status of the process

process: For negotiation: draft the demand or response, conduct rounds, log positions and counteroffers.
For mediation: select the mediator, prepare the mediation brief, attend the session.
For arbitration: file the demand, conduct discovery, prepare for hearing, attend.
For litigation: file the complaint or answer, conduct discovery, prepare for trial.
Track all actions and costs in the process log.

steps.description: Document the settlement or outcome of the dispute.

outputs.name: settlement-agreement
outputs.desc: The settlement agreement or judgment documenting the outcome

outputs.name: dispute-resolution-record
outputs.desc: Complete record of the dispute from claim through resolution

process: Draft the settlement agreement with all terms (payment, release, confidentiality, non-admission).
Obtain all required signatures.
If litigated, record the judgment or verdict.
Compile the complete dispute resolution record.

description: Draft, circulate, approve, and file board resolutions for corporate actions requiring board authorization.

steps.description: Identify the corporate action requiring board approval and determine the resolution type.

inputs.name: proposed-action
inputs.desc: The corporate action that needs board authorization

inputs.name: governance-requirements
inputs.desc: Bylaws or governance rules specifying what requires board action

outputs.name: resolution-type
outputs.desc: Type of resolution needed (ordinary, special, written consent, unanimous)

outputs.name: approval-requirements
outputs.desc: Quorum, voting threshold, and notice requirements

process: Determine whether the proposed action requires board approval per the bylaws or governing documents.
Identify the resolution type based on the action (officer appointment, contract approval, budget, merger).
Determine the quorum and voting threshold required.
Identify the notice requirements and lead time.

steps.description: Draft the board resolution with the required recitals and operative clauses.

outputs.name: draft-resolution
outputs.desc: The draft resolution ready for circulation

outputs.name: supporting-materials
outputs.desc: Any supporting documents needed for the board's review

process: Draft the resolution with recitals (background facts) and operative clauses (the action authorized).
Include the effective date and any conditions.
Attach or reference any supporting materials the board needs to review.
Circulate the draft for legal review before sending to the board.

steps.description: Circulate the resolution to the board and coordinate the review and comment period.

outputs.name: board-feedback
outputs.desc: Comments and questions received from board members

outputs.name: revised-resolution
outputs.desc: The resolution revised to incorporate board feedback

process: Distribute the draft resolution and supporting materials to all board members.
Allow the review period specified in the bylaws.
Collect and consolidate comments and questions.
Revise the resolution to address the feedback.

steps.description: Present the resolution for vote and record the outcome.

inputs.name: board-feedback
inputs.desc: Any remaining feedback or discussion points

outputs.name: vote-record
outputs.desc: Record of the vote: for, against, abstain, and whether the threshold was met

outputs.name: executed-resolution
outputs.desc: The resolution signed by the appropriate officers

process: Present the resolution at the board meeting or distribute for written consent.
Record each director's vote (for, against, abstain).
Determine whether the required threshold was met.
If approved, have the resolution signed by the secretary or chair.

steps.description: File the executed resolution in the corporate records and distribute as needed.

outputs.name: filed-resolution
outputs.desc: The resolution filed in the corporate minute book

outputs.name: board-resolution-record
outputs.desc: Complete record including the action, resolution, vote, and filing

process: File the executed resolution in the corporate minute book or records system.
Distribute copies to the parties who need to act on the resolution.
File any required external filings (state filings, SEC, bank) referencing the resolution.
Produce the complete board resolution record.
